title: God was silent.
paragraphs:
God was silent.
And it almost broke him.

Psalm 22:2 is not a soft prayer. It is a desperate cry:
“O my God, I cry in the daytime, but You do not hear; and in the night season, and am not silent.”
Read that again.

Daytime.
Night season.
No answer.

This is not unbelief.
This is faith under pressure.
Because even in the silence… David still says, “my God.”
That’s the tension most people don’t understand.

You can be faithful… and still feel unheard.
You can be praying… and still feel abandoned.
You can love God… and still wrestle with His silence.
And if you’ve ever been there—this Psalm is your language.
But here’s what we miss…

Psalm 22 does not end in silence.
It moves from anguish… to assurance.
And even deeper—this Psalm is not just David’s cry.
It is Christ’s cry.

On the cross, Jesus reached into Psalm 22 and pulled it into history:
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matthew 27:46)
Do you see it?

The silence you fear…
Jesus stepped into it.

The abandonment you dread…
He carried it.

The judgment your sin deserved…
He absorbed it.
Because here is the truth we don’t like to face:

Our greatest problem was never God’s silence.
It was our sin.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
“Your iniquities have separated you from your God.” (Isaiah 59:2)

We were not just ignored.
We were separated.
But God did not stay distant.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
That’s the Gospel.

Jesus took the silence of judgment…
So we could receive the voice of grace.
And here’s where it shifts—

God’s silence is not always punishment.
Sometimes it is preparation.
Sometimes it is purification.
Sometimes it is an invitation to deeper trust.
“Be still, and know that I am God.” (Psalm 46:10)
Stillness is uncomfortable.

Because it strips away distractions.
It exposes what we run to.
It reveals whether we want God… or just what God gives.
Let’s be honest—

Some of us only pray hard when we need something.
Some of us only seek Him when life hurts.
Some of us love His hand… more than His heart.
And silence confronts that.
But listen—

Silence is not absence.
Delay is not denial.
And quiet does not mean God is not working.
“The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise… but is patient with you.” (2 Peter 3:9)

What feels like delay…
May actually be mercy.

What feels like distance…
May actually be formation.

Because God is not just trying to answer your prayer—
He is shaping your heart.
And that takes time.
Even Jesus walked through it.

Hebrews tells us:
“Though He was a Son, yet He learned obedience by the things which He suffered.” (Hebrews 5:8)

If the Son of God walked through suffering…
Why do we expect a shortcut?
But here is the hope you cannot afford to miss—
Psalm 22 does not end in despair.
It ends in victory.
“All the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the Lord.” (Psalm 22:27)

From silence… to salvation.
From suffering… to redemption.
From the cross… to the resurrection.
Friday was silent.
But Sunday spoke louder than death.
“He is not here; for He is risen.” (Matthew 28:6)
So if you are in a silent season right now…

Do not quit.
Do not numb it.
Do not run.
Stay.

Cry if you must.
Wrestle if you must.
But keep saying, “my God.”

Because the same Jesus who entered silence…
Also conquered it.

And if you belong to Him—
Silence is not your ending.
Resurrection is.
